Not by default. December 22nd falls inside the year-end code freeze (Dec 15 to Jan 5) while Finance runs the annual close. No production release may go out in that window, hotfixes included, unless a lead in #fin-eng signs off in the channel first.

Your options:

1. **Get sign-off.** Ask a lead in #fin-eng to approve the release in the channel. Since Finance wants the fix, they may be willing. Get it in writing in the channel before you tag.
2. **Release before the freeze.** Tag by Dec 14. Today is Oct 5, so there's plenty of time.
3. **Wait until after Jan 5.**

If you go ahead on the 22nd, the normal process still applies:
- Tag `vYYYY.MM.N` from main (for example `v2026.12.1`). CI publishes it, so don't publish by hand.
- Complete the PR template's release checklist first.
- Staging is promoted automatically. Production needs a manual approval in the CI UI from someone on the billing team.
- Dec 22 is a Tuesday, so the Friday-after-14:00-UTC avoidance doesn't apply.
- Ship any database migrations in the same release as the code that needs them.

I can't tell from the repo whether sign-off has already been given. That has to come from #fin-eng.
